hearn.title: Computer Graphics with OpenGL
hearn.authors: Donald Hearn, M. Pauline Baker and Warren R. Carithers

deberg.title: Computational Geometry: Algorithms and Applications
deberg.authors: Mark de Berg, Otfried Cheong, Marc van Kreveld and Mark Overmars

introduction-and-applications.why: A survey of graphics applications, from CAD to simulation and visualisation.

graphics-hardware-and-software.read: Chapter 2: Computer Graphics Hardware; Chapter 3: Computer Graphics Software
graphics-hardware-and-software.why: Displays, frame buffers, GPUs and graphics APIs.

output-primitives-and-line-drawing.read: Chapters 4 and 6: Graphics Output Primitives; Implementation Algorithms for Graphics Primitives
output-primitives-and-line-drawing.why: DDA, Bresenham's line algorithm, the midpoint circle algorithm and antialiasing.

polygons-and-filling.read: Chapter 4 (polygon fill areas) and Chapter 8: Two-Dimensional Viewing (clipping)
polygons-and-filling.why: Polygon types, inside-outside tests, fill algorithms and clipping.

geometric-transformations.read: Chapters 7 and 9: Two-Dimensional and Three-Dimensional Geometric Transformations
geometric-transformations.why: Translation, rotation, scaling, homogeneous coordinates and composite transformations.

3d-modelling-and-rendering.read: Chapters 10–18 (viewing, visible-surface detection, illumination and surface rendering)
3d-modelling-and-rendering.why: Projection, the z-buffer, Phong and Gouraud shading and texture mapping.

computational-geometry.read: Chapters 1, 2, 7, 9 and 13: Convex Hulls; Line Segment Intersection; Voronoi Diagrams; Delaunay Triangulations; Robot Motion Planning
computational-geometry.why: The standard text on computational geometry, including robot motion planning.
